finding.claim: Blind SSRF: POST /profile/avatar passes the client-supplied avatarUrl to axios.get without a host, IP, or redirect check. Only an https:// prefix is enforced, and only on the initial URL.
finding.source: req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10), supplied by any client that can reach port 3000 in a JSON request body; no authentication.
finding.sink: axios.get(url, {responseType: 'arraybuffer'}) at server.js:14, an outbound HTTP(S) request from the server.

trace.note: Route POST /profile/avatar registered; express.json() at line 5 parses the body.
url = req.body.avatarUrl, taken unchanged from the request body.
Only typeof string and startsWith('https://') are checked; a 400 is returned otherwise.

axios.get follows the attacker URL, including redirects (axios default in Node, not verifiable in repo). No timeout or size cap. Redirects to http://169.254.169.254 or internal hosts are not re-checked.
Only img.data.length is returned, so the response is a size oracle. Non-2xx responses throw unhandled at line 14, leaving the client hanging, which gives a port and service-existence oracle.

finding.guards_checked: typeof string check (line 11): blocks non-strings only. startsWith('https://') (line 11): case-sensitive, does not restrict host, IP, or port, and does not cover redirects. No allow-list, no DNS/IP range check, no redirect policy, no try/catch or timeout around line 14. Express/axios versions not present in repo, so redirect default and unhandled-rejection behavior are unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. server.js:11 only checks typeof string and a case-sensitive startsWith('https://'), which does not restrict host, IP, port, or redirects. No allow-list, IP-range check, redirect policy, or try/catch/timeout exists around server.js:14.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10, unauthenticated POST /profile/avatar at server.js:9) reaches axios.get at server.js:14 with only an https:// prefix check at server.js:11, so any https host or internal https service is reachable. Two caveats: the response is returned as a byte length (server.js:15), so it is a size oracle rather than fully blind, and the redirect-following behavior is an axios default not verifiable from this repo, but neither changes the verdict because the initial-URL SSRF is unguarded.

finding.claim: Unhandled rejection on axios failure: no try/catch around the axios call, so errors from line 14 are not converted to an HTTP response. Availability issue related to SSRF-1, not a separate SSRF.
finding.sink: Unhandled promise rejection from axios.get at server.js:14; may crash the process depending on Node version and Express version (unverified).

trace.note: axios.get rejects on non-2xx, network error, or timeout.
Express 4 does not catch rejections from async handlers, so no response is sent.

verdict.guard_found: none: server.js:14 has no try/catch and nothing wraps the axios.get call. The only check is server.js:11, a typeof/startsWith("https://") check that does not restrict the host.
verdict.reason: The cited lines exist and match the claim (source at server.js:10, sink at server.js:14, no try/catch), but the trace's key step, that Express does not catch async rejections at server.js:9, depends on the Express major version, and no package.json or lockfile exists in the directory to confirm it is Express 4 rather than Express 5. Because that premise is unverified, I mark trace_ok=false and the verdict UNVERIFIABLE; the separate SSRF-1 finding is not affected by this note.
